source_statement: A semicircle is inscribed in another semicircle if the smaller semicircle’s diameter is a chord of the larger semicircle, and the smaller semicircle’s arc is tangent to the diameter of the larger semicircle. Semicircle S1 is inscribed in a semicircle S2 , which is inscribed in another semicircle S3 . The radii of S1 and S3 are 1 and 10, respectively, and the diameters of S1 and S3 are parallel. The endpoints of the diameter of S3 are A and B, and S2 ’s arc is tangent to AB at C. Compute AC · CB. S3 S2 S1 A C B

clause_ledger.source: S3 radius 10 and diameter endpoints A,B
clause_ledger.dsl: fixed horizontal diameter A=(0,0), B=(20,0), Gamma3 centered at (10,0)

clause_ledger.source: S2 inscribed in S3 and tangent to AB at C
clause_ledger.dsl: tangency to AB gives O2=(cx,r2); U,V are constructed as the two endpoints of the radius-r2 chord of S3 centered at O2 (the chord direction is perpendicular to O3O2), and the original outer-incidence constraints remain

clause_ledger.source: S1 radius1 inscribed in S2 with diameter parallel to S3
clause_ledger.dsl: construct U1,V1 as the horizontal diameter endpoints of the radius-1 S1; O1 remains free subject to the original S2-incidence and diameter-tangency constraints
